names: UCSF Mission Bay Building 23B Parking Structure
summary: UCSF's nine-level, 822-space Building 23B Parking Structure at 1650 3rd Street in Mission Bay, on Block 23 between 3rd and 4th Streets; the Regents approved its $23.3M budget in November 2003 with construction slated to run March 2004 to July 2005. Designed by Stanley Saitowitz/Natoma Architects, its original channel-glass facade was replaced in 2021 with IwamotoScott's 'Cellular Origami' aluminum-panel facade.

milestones.text: UC Regents' Committee on Grounds and Buildings and Committee on Finance approve the $23,298,000 budget and external financing for the Mission Bay Building 23B Parking Structure Project (822 spaces on nine levels plus 52 surface spaces, Block 23)
Construction slated to begin, per the 2003 Regents budget item
Garage slated for completion alongside the Mission Bay Block 20 campus housing project, per the 2003 Regents budget item's projected schedule (an actual opening announcement was not found)
Original channel-glass exterior facade replaced with IwamotoScott Architecture's 'Cellular Origami' aluminum-panel facade

open_questions: No source confirms the garage's actual completion date; the 2005-07 milestone above is the 2003 budget item's projected schedule, not a completion announcement -- a UC construction schedule commonly slips, so this date is flagged approximate.

The 2003 Regents item describes a nine-level, 822-space structure; this record's own geometry file cites OpenStreetMap tagging of 8 levels -- not reconciled here, since OSM levels and the Regents' 'nine levels (including a half level at the top)' description are plausibly the same building described two ways.
Exact capacity today (after any reconfiguration) is not confirmed by any source found, per this record's own geometry file notes.
The general contractor for the original 2004-2005 construction was not identified in this pass.
